samples.summary: A write that fails during compression bypasses `onWriteFailure`, so the chip keeps promising "Saved to this device" for a document nothing stored
samples.evidence: `saveSnapshot` (l.620), `appendChange` (l.662) and `saveMeta` (l.709) all do `await deflate(...)` *before* entering `withQuotaRetry`, which is the only place `reportWriteFailure` is called. Any rejection from `deflate`/`through` — `new CompressionStream('gzip')` throwing on a runtime that lacks it (Safari <16.4, Firefox <113), or a stream error — therefore propagates to the SDK, which the file's own docs say swallows store errors, while `DurableYorkieProvider`'s `writesFailing` latch is never set. `durable` stays `true` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:195), so `deriveSyncState` reports `saved-locally` and the tooltip says the unsent work is on disk when nothing was ever written. The design's stated rule is that a store failing its writes must lower `durable`; this is the one failure class that escapes it. Moving the `deflate` inside `withQuotaRetry` (or wrapping it in `reportWriteFailure`) closes it.

samples.summary: `offlineUserId()` is one device-wide slot, so a purge triggered by one account can delete another account's entries and archives
samples.evidence: `offlineUserId()` returns a single module/`localStorage` value, last written by whichever `OfflineRuntime` mounted most recently (offline-runtime.tsx:66) — it is not scoped to the tab or to the account that initiated the action. `purgeOfflineDocuments` (l.412) and `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (l.506) both build their store from it, and `isOfflineUser` (l.116) answers from it. With two accounts on one device (a second tab signing in as B while tab 1 still runs as A, or a session that expired without a logout so the mirror still names A), an action taken in tab 1 purges under B's scope; `removeMember`/`deleteWorkspace` pass `{ dropArchives: true }` (api/workspaces.ts:167), and an archive is by this feature's own design the only copy of work the server never took. The window is narrow because `OfflineRuntime` rewrites the mirror on mount, but nothing ties a purge to the account that actually requested it.

samples.summary: `release()` deletes the election entry before the Web Lock is actually free, so an immediate re-acquire for the same document can be refused and never retried
samples.evidence: `release()` does `elections.delete(name)` then `releaseLock()` (l.456-462). `releaseLock` only resolves the promise the `navigator.locks.request` callback is parked on (l.360-381); the manager frees the name when that promise *settles*, which is a later microtask/task. A remount for the same document in the same tab (route away and straight back, or any unmount/mount pair) runs the cleanup and then immediately issues a fresh `request(name, { ifAvailable: true })` under a brand-new `elections` entry. If the manager has not yet observed the release, the new request resolves `undefined`, `useDurableDocument` latches non-durable for that open (`latched`/`decision` never re-run — the effect deps did not change), and nothing retries: the document silently loses durability for the rest of that open while the lock name is in fact free. The module's own doc comment describes exactly this failure mode for the StrictMode case and guards only that one.

samples.summary: `purgeOfflineDocuments` wraps the whole loop in one try/catch, so one failing id silently skips every remaining id
samples.evidence: The `for (const id of documentIds)` loop at l.418 sits inside a single `try`; a rejection from `store.purgeDocument` on the first id jumps to the `catch` at l.423 and the rest of `documentIds` is never purged. The callers are the bulk paths — `deleteDocuments` (api/documents.ts:214) and `deleteWorkspace`/`removeMember` with `dropArchives: true` (api/workspaces.ts:113,167), which can pass dozens of ids — so a single transient IndexedDB failure leaves local copies (and, on the access-loss paths, archives) of documents the server has already deleted or revoked on disk until the thirty-day sweep, with only a `console.warn`. Per-id try/catch would bound the damage to the one id that failed.

samples.summary: `durableClientKey()` is called during render, so a device secret can be re-minted into `localStorage` right after the erase deliberately forgot it
samples.evidence: `clientKey: durable && userId ? durableClientKey(userId, docKey) : undefined` runs on every render of a durable document. `durableClientKey` → `deviceSecret()` (durable-session.ts:~300) reads, touches (`localStorage.setItem`) and, when nothing is stored, *mints and persists* a new salt. `eraseOfflineData` ends with `forgetDeviceSecret(userId)` (offline-erase.ts:39) precisely so no salt for that account is left on a shared device, but the durable client is deliberately left mounted across the erase, and this hook subscribes to the preference (`useOfflinePersistenceEnabled`) — so any later render for the same subject writes a fresh salt back for an account whose data was just erased. It also makes a synchronous `localStorage` read/write part of every render of every durable editor.

samples.summary: `rehydrateArchive` hands `Document.fromBytes` the SDK store key instead of the document key
samples.evidence: `Document.fromBytes<R>(summary.docKey, stored.snapshot)` uses `summary.docKey`, which is whatever the SDK passed to `remove()` — the scoped store key `apiKey/clientKey/docKey` (see `documentIdOf` right above, which strips exactly those segments, and the archive seeded as `'/wb:u1:note-7/note-7'` in offline-copy.test.ts). The rebuilt document therefore carries a key that is not its document key. It is benign if `fromBytes` merely constructs and applies, but if the SDK validates the key against the snapshot header it throws, `rehydrateArchive` answers `undefined`, and every archive written under a scoped key reports `refused: 'unreadable'` — the one path the recovery feature exists for. No test rehydrates a scoped key, so neither behaviour is pinned.

samples.summary: `void pending.then(...)` has no rejection handler on either the body or the cleanup
samples.evidence: Both `void pending.then((handle) => {...})` (l.207) and the cleanup's `void pending.then((handle) => handle?.release())` (l.219) attach only fulfilment handlers. `acquireDurableSession` is defensive today (the lock request carries its own `.catch`), so a rejection needs the function itself to throw — but if it ever does, this becomes an unhandled rejection inside a React effect rather than a fall back to non-durable.

finding.summary: A write that fails during compression bypasses `onWriteFailure`, so the chip keeps promising "Saved to this device" for a document nothing stored

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. `saveSnapshot` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:620), `appendChange` (:662) and `saveMeta` (:709) each `await deflate(...)` before entering `withQuotaRetry`. `deflate` (:290-292) constructs `new CompressionStream("gzip")` and awaits `through` (:252-287), so both a constructor throw and a stream error reject outside the retry wrapper. A grep over packages/frontend/src shows `reportWriteFailure` is invoked only at :410 (refuseIfDisabled, which runs before the deflate) and :1411/:1416/:1422 (inside withQuotaRetry) — so a compression failure reaches no failure reporting. On the consumer side, `onWriteFailure` is the sole channel that sets `writesFailing` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:161-171), and `durable: !lost && !writesFailing && !persistDisabled && !unreportable` (:195) plus the lapse ladder (:216-226) therefore keep reporting durability; the store is passed straight to the SDK provider (:49, :229-236) with no wrapper that catches store errors. No feature detection for CompressionStream exists anywhere in packages/frontend, so nothing makes the path unreachable. Real correctness defect: an error path that leaves latched UI state asserting work is on disk when nothing was written.

With two accounts on one device (a second tab signing in as B while tab 1 still runs as A, or a session that expired without a logout so the mirror still names A), an action taken in tab 1 purges under B's scope; `removeMember`/`deleteWorkspace` pass `{ dropArchives: true }` (api/workspaces.ts:167), and an archive is by this feature's own design the only copy of work the server never took. verdict.reason: The cited code exists as described in substance: offlineUserId() (offline-erase.ts:98-107) resolves the purge scope from ambient state — a module-level signedInUserId with a device-wide localStorage mirror (LAST_USER_KEY, written at offline-erase.ts:75-95) as fallback — and both purgeOfflineDocuments (offline-erase.ts:408-416) and purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments (offline-erase.ts:506-514) build their WafflebaseDocStore from it, taking no account argument from the caller. isOfflineUser (offline-erase.ts:116-118) answers from the same slot, and removeMember (api/workspaces.ts:159,167) and deleteWorkspace (api/workspaces.ts:127,136) purge with {dropArchives: true}, which destroys the archive the feature calls the only copy of work the server never took. Part of the reviewer's mechanism is inaccurate: signedInUserId is per-JS-realm (per tab) and takes precedence over the mirror (offline-erase.ts:99-101), and every purge-capable surface (workspace-settings.tsx:133,182; document-list.tsx:530) sits under PrivateRoute (App.tsx:139-187), which mounts OfflineRuntime with that tab's own String(me.id) (PrivateRoute.tsx:58 -> offline-runtime.tsx:66) — so the literal "tab 1 purges under B's scope" story does not hold for a tab that rendered the shell. But that mount is conditional on offlineInPlay = supportsClientKey() || preference(me.id) (PrivateRoute.tsx:28-30), and the pin is @yorkie-js/react 0.7.22 (packages/frontend/package.json:66) against MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23 (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,76-82), so supportsClientKey() is false here and a signed-in account without the preference sets no tab-local identity at all; offlineUserId() then returns the device-wide mirror left by another account whose session expired without a logout (the mirror is only cleared on a completed logout erase, offline-erase.ts:84-88,337), and that account's entries and archives are purged with dropArchives: true. Separately, purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments scopes its store from offlineUserId() while taking its authority listing from the ambient cookie (offline-runtime.tsx:177-183), so a stale cached `me` against a switched session drops archives on a 403 for an account that did not request anything. No guard ties a purge to the requesting account, so I have no named ground to refute on; uncertainty about how often the mis-scoping actually destroys content that should have survived is expressed in confidence, not by dropping the finding.
